title: Adversaries' Mosaic-tradition reply — oral law claim still falls under Christ's verdict
source_text: XXVII. Respondunt adversarii, Christum & Apostolos non reprehendere traditiones, quas Judaei acceperant a Mose & Prophetis, sed traditiones acceptas a quibusdam recentioribus, quae quidem traditiones partim inanes erant, partim cum Scripturis repugnabant: Sed aliam esse rationem traditionum Ecclesiae Romanae, quas illi scilicet a Christo & Apostolis acceperunt. Sed contra sciendum est, traditiones illas, quas Christus exagitat ut doctrinas hominum, pro traditionibus Mosaicis & Propheticis fuisse venditatas. Nam Judaeorum Rabbini, in eo majorum suorum vestigiis insistentes, traditiones suas vocant thorah shebbal peh, quasi dicas, legem oralem, nempe quia volunt illas ore tenus a Mose acceptas, qui illas in monte Sinai ab ipso Deo habuerit, non minus quam legem scriptam, cui proinde volunt illas authoritate pares esse. Jam autem Christi tempore Judaeorum Doctores erant Ecclesiae Doctores & Magistri: siquidem nulla tum erat vera Dei Ecclesia nisi apud Judaeos. Cum ergo nihilominus Christus aperte rejiciat, & pro doctrinis hominum habeat traditiones quas extra Scripturam proferebant, licet ab antiquis illas accepissent, adeoque ab ipso Mose traditas gloriarentur, quam fidem facient hodierni Pontificiorum Doctores traditiones illas, quas se ab ipso Christo & Apostolis ejus per manus patrum suorum accepisse se jactant, revera esse instituta Christi & Apostolorum, non vero humana inventa? Et certe cum inde pateat Ecclesiae magistros in eo posse falli, & pro divinis obtrudere dogmata & praecepta quae mere humana sunt, Inde quoque sequitur nullum extra Scripturam sacram certum Dei verbum reperiri. Etenim, si quod tale verbum Dei exstaret, ab Ecclesiae praepositis accipiendum esset, nec majori authoritate nobis commendaretur.
pass_a_gloss: The adversaries answer that Christ and the Apostles do not rebuke the traditions which the Jews had received from Moses and the Prophets, but traditions received from certain more recent men — traditions which were partly empty and partly contradictory to the Scriptures; but that the case of the Roman Church's traditions is different, which they of course received from Christ and the Apostles. But against this it must be known that those traditions which Christ attacks as doctrines of men were being marketed as Mosaic and Prophetic traditions. For the Jewish Rabbis, following in this the footsteps of their ancestors, call their traditions thorah shebbal peh — as if to say, the oral law — namely because they want them received by living voice from Moses, who had them on Mount Sinai from God Himself, no less than the written law, to which accordingly they want them equal in authority. Now at Christ's time the Jewish doctors were the Church's doctors and teachers, since then there was no true Church of God except among the Jews. When therefore Christ nevertheless openly rejects and treats as doctrines of men the traditions they brought forward outside Scripture, even though they had received them from the ancients and boasted they were handed down from Moses himself — what faith will today's Pontifical doctors create that those traditions which they boast they received from Christ Himself and His Apostles through their fathers' hands are truly Christ's and the Apostles' institutes, and not human inventions? And certainly, since from this it is plain that the Church's teachers can err in this and thrust forward as divine dogmas and precepts that are merely human, it also follows that no certain word of God is found outside sacred Scripture. For if any such word of God existed, it would have to be received from the Church's overseers, and it would not be recommended to us with greater authority.
pass_b_english: Rome replies: Christ condemned only later, empty, or Scripture-contradicting Jewish traditions — not Mosaic/Prophetic ones — and Rome's traditions come from Christ and the Apostles.

Counter: the traditions Christ attacks as human doctrines were sold as Mosaic and Prophetic. Rabbis call them thorah shebbal peh (oral law), claiming Moses received them viva voce on Sinai equal in authority with the written law.
In Christ's day those Jewish doctors were the Church's only teachers — there was no true Church of God except among the Jews.

Yet Christ still rejects their extra-Scriptural traditions as human doctrines despite ancient/Mosaic pedigree. So why trust today's Roman doctors when they claim hand-to-hand receipt from Christ and the Apostles?

Church teachers can err and push merely human dogmas as divine; therefore no certain word of God stands outside sacred Scripture — for any such word would still have to come through fallible overseers, with no greater warrant.
